sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: A bag has 2 red and 3 blue marbles. What is the theoretical probability of drawing red?

steps: Identify the favorable outcomes and the total possible outcomes.
Write the probability as a reduced fraction, or use it to predict or evaluate a count.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: A fair coin is flipped and a spinner with 6 equal sections numbered 1 to 6 is spun. What is the probability of getting heads on the coin and landing on 4 on the spinner?
A pizza is made by choosing one topping from 5 options and one crust from 6 options. How many different pizzas are possible?

A probability model predicts a fair 10-section spinner lands on a chosen section about 13 times in 130 spins. A simulation of 130 spins landed on that section 15 times. How does the simulated count compare to the model's prediction?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: An event has a probability of 1. How would you describe how likely the event is to happen?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A spinner was spun 20 times and landed on blue 8 times. Based on this experiment, what is the experimental probability of landing on blue?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A bag has 5 red, 7 blue, and 9 green marbles. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the theoretical probability of drawing red, P(red)?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
